name: the shop's sale: every policy at the same numbers, yours first
why: The post's comparison: the same capacity and spike, and only the policy changes. Answered and p50 are the post's numbers from shed_sim.py; back to normal is the first 10 s window after the spike from which every window answers 90% or more; served to nobody is work finished after its client gave up. The three outcome shares per policy are pinned in index.test.ts, since a chart fixture checks its frame and not its data.

columns.label: What it does at these numbers

rows.text: Do not retry, or bound the queue so nothing waits past the timeout.
When everyone is timing out, each person sends 4 tries in 10 s: 70/s times 4 is 280/s against 100/s, so the queue cannot drain. In this run it did not.
69.0% answered instead of 8.4%, and 0.0% wait for nothing instead of 91.6%. Back to normal: at once.
Or add workers for the spike.
13 workers is the fewest whose capacity is over the 150/s spike. The capacity planner sizes them for a wait target.
